issues.legal_issue: An allottee with a long-term, heritable and transferable interest in premises may qualify as their owner in relation to a tenant for the purpose of seeking eviction on the ground of the landlord’s reasonable requirement.
material_facts: The landlord held an allotment under which he had a heritable and transferable right to possess the premises for 99 years.
The landlord could let the premises and receive rental income, subject to the allotment terms and obtaining the society’s written consent.
The landlord let the premises to the tenant and sought eviction for his own reasonable requirement.
The landlord’s interest was a sublease from a society that itself held a long-term lease.
issues.conclusion: The landlord was the owner of the premises in relation to the tenant for purposes of the Act and could seek eviction on the reasonable-requirement ground if its other conditions were established.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2 and 13(1)(ff) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, the landlord must be the owner to seek eviction for his own occupation. Ownership is a complex of rights and need not include every incident of full or absolute ownership; the relevant question is whether the claimant has a superior right or interest against the tenant. The Court referred to Salmond on Jurisprudence, 12th edition, Chapter 8, and Sections 87 and 89 of the West Bengal Co-operative Societies Act, 1983. An allottee with a heritable and transferable right to possess, let and receive income from premises has a superior interest against the tenant and qualifies as owner for this purpose.

rule.if: eviction_suit_for_landlord_occupation and allottee_has_long_term_heritable_interest and allottee_can_let_and_receive_rent and allottee_has_superior_interest_to_tenant

predicates.eviction_suit_for_landlord_occupation: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant so that the landlord may occupy the premises.
predicates.allottee_has_long_term_heritable_interes: The claimant holds an allotment that gives a long-term interest in the premises capable of inheritance and transfer.
predicates.allottee_can_let_and_receive_rent: The claimant is entitled to let the premises and receive the rental income, subject to applicable conditions.
predicates.allottee_has_superior_interest_to_tenant: The claimant’s rights in the premises are superior to the tenant’s rights.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeking the premises for personal occupation has a long-term heritable interest, may let the premises and receive rent, and holds a superior interest to the tenant, the landlord qualifies as owner against that tenant.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may not overturn an eviction decree solely on a title objection that was not pleaded or tried, and must decide the appeal on the pleadings and merits.
material_facts: The tenant did not dispute the landlord’s title or ownership in the written statement or at trial.
No issue concerning ownership was framed at trial.
The first appellate court raised the ownership question and reversed the eviction decree solely on that basis without examining the reasonable-requirement claim.
The High Court affirmed that decision without examining the merits of the eviction claim.
issues.conclusion: The appellate judgments were set aside and the case was remanded for fresh disposal of the tenant’s appeal on the merits, on the basis that the landlord was the owner as pleaded.
issues.legal_principle: A case is to be decided on the pleadings; where title was not challenged and no issue on ownership was framed, the appellate courts could not set aside the decree solely on that unraised question. The Supreme Court set aside those judgments and remanded the appeal for consideration on its merits. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this procedural ruling.

rule.if: appeal_from_eviction_decree and tenant_did_not_dispute_title_at_trial and no_ownership_issue_framed and appellate_court_reversed_solely_on_title

predicates.appeal_from_eviction_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree granting eviction.
predicates.tenant_did_not_dispute_title_at_trial: The tenant did not challenge the landlord’s title in the pleadings or at trial.
predicates.no_ownership_issue_framed: The trial court did not frame an issue about the landlord’s ownership.
predicates.appellate_court_reversed_solely_on_title: The appellate court overturned the decree based only on the landlord’s title without deciding the eviction claim on its merits.

issues.definition: When an appeal from an eviction decree turns solely on a title objection not raised or tried, the case is remanded for decision on its merits.
